issues.description: `Course.ratings` element type is inconsistent: the problem statement and template define `ratings` as `[Int]` (star ratings 1–5), but the solution defines it as `[Double]` and the initializer takes `[Double]`. This breaks the expected type contract for `Course` and can cause compilation/test failures when code expects `[Int]`.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts to use integer star ratings: change the solution to `var ratings: [Int]` and `init(..., ratings: [Int])`. Keep `addRating(stars: Int)` appending `Int`, and convert to `Double` only when computing the average in `getAverageRating()`.

issues.description: `Course` initializer parameter type is inconsistent with the specification: the problem statement shows `Course(name:..., instructor:..., ratings: [])` where `ratings` is `[Int]`, but the solution defines `init(name:instructor:ratings:)` with `ratings: [Double]`. This mismatched constructor signature can prevent students/tests from instantiating `Course` as specified.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution initializer signature to `init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int])` to match the problem statement/template (or update the problem statement/template to `[Double]`, but prefer `[Int]` since `addRating(stars:)` accepts `Int`).
